sources.entry: Corectl App for macOS - Corectl App is a macOS Status bar App which works like a wrapper around the corectl command line tool corectld to control the server runtime process.

summary.one_liner: Corectl App is a macOS status bar app that wraps the corectl command-line tool and its corectld server daemon, letting you start, monitor, and restart the server that runs CoreOS VMs on the native macOS Hypervisor framework.
summary.what_it_does: The app sits in the macOS status bar and controls the corectld server runtime process rather than running VMs itself. Its menu shows whether the server is running, the server version, and the active VMs, and it can restart the server. It can also check for a new app version and check for and download a new corectl version. It can fetch the latest CoreOS ISO images into ~/.coreos/images for sharing between VMs. The README says a local Docker registry runs at 192.168.64.1:5000 with images stored under ~/.coreos/registry/. The README states the app is very light on system resources, and that corectld uses little when no VMs are running.
use_cases: Run CoreOS virtual machines on a Mac without VirtualBox
Start and restart the corectld server from the menu bar
See which VMs are active on the Mac
Download the latest CoreOS ISO images
Host a shared local Docker registry for VMs
Run a single-node or multi-node Kubernetes cluster on macOS
how_to_run: Download corectl_app.dmg from the Releases page
Open the DMG and drag the app to /Applications
Start Corectl from /Applications and enter your Mac user password when prompted
notable: Wraps the corectl CLI in a status bar app with a menu for server status and VM listing
Uses the native macOS Hypervisor framework, so no VirtualBox or similar virtualisation software is needed
Includes a local Docker registry shared among all VMs
Can fetch and store CoreOS ISO images for reuse across VMs
Used by the TheNewNormal CoreOS and Kubernetes-on-macOS projects
caveats: Requires macOS 10.10.3 Yosemite or later and a Mac from 2010 or later
Needs libev installed through Homebrew until qcow-tool works as a standalone binary
Asks for the Mac user password on each start because corectl runs as root for networking
